subject: SIG: RTO/RPO detail request — KV failover and warm cache timings
messages:
From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@NimbusFin.com>

Cc: Nimbus Fin - Compliance Team <compliance@nimbusfin.com>, Sara Nguyen <s.nguyen@nimbusfin.com>

Subject: SIG questionnaire follow-up — RTO/RPO specifics

Neha —

Thanks for taking our SIG submission earlier this week. The compliance team had a couple of follow-ups specifically around the RTO/RPO evidence we received. Two narrow asks to unblock our internal review: 

1) For the KV cache and prefix caching you reference in the response, what is the measured recovery time (RTO) from a cold start versus a warm cache for our expected 95th percentile request size (approx 1.5k tokens)?

2) In a region failover (primary -> secondary) scenario, can you provide the sequence of automated steps and an estimate for the additional latency introduced while KV caches rehydrate? We need this to model the expected tail latency for our SLA mapping.

We also noted the snapshot file in the materials but couldn't find a short excerpt of the runbook that maps KV cache rehydration to RTO milestones. If you can provide a short runbook excerpt plus any test timestamps you used, that would be ideal.

Targeting our compliance board meeting next Thursday — appreciate anything you can get to us before EOD Wednesday (9/8).

Best,
Tom
Senior Compliance Manager
Nimbus Financial

--

Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire follow-up — RTO/RPO specifics

Hi Tom —

Thanks for the clear asks. We're on it. Short answers up front:

- Cold start RTO (full service restart + KV cache empty): typically 6–9 minutes to start serving at full throughput for 1.5k token requests in our us-west region; 95th-percentile token latency stabilizes within ~8 minutes in our standard test harness.
- Warm-cache RTO (cache present or snapshot restored): ~45–120 seconds to reach steady-state 95th percentile for that request size, depending on cache hit patterns.

I'm pulling the runbook excerpt and test timestamps now and will send a compiled packet (snapshot PDF + runbook excerpt + control mapping) by EOD Wednesday. Diego will attach the raw test logs and the small runbook excerpt that maps the KV rehydration checkpoints to measurable RTO milestones.

One note: our measured numbers assume the standard autoscaling policy and a pre-warmed pool size equal to the dedicated baseline. If Nimbus wants a hardened SLA with shorter RTOs, we can propose reserved warm pool configurations — happy to include options.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Manager, Compliance & Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_rto_snapshot_20260907.pdf (will follow)

Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire follow-up — RTO/RPO specifics

Tom / Sara / Compliance team —

Attached is the packet we discussed:
- redwood_rto_snapshot_20260907.pdf (summary of p50/p95/p99 across cold and warm runs)
- kv-failover-runbook-excerpt.txt (runbook excerpt showing detection -> failover -> cache seed -> validation checkpoints)
- sig_control_map_v3.xlsx (SIG control map with references to SOC2 sections and evidence IDs)

Key highlights:
- Cold-start to full throughput: 6–9 minutes (95th percentile stabilizes ~8 minutes). Test harness logs included in the snapshot show raw timestamps.
- Warm-cache steady-state: 45–120 seconds to converge to expected p95 for 1.5k token requests depending on traffic mix; typical median ~70s in our tests.
- Region failover sequence: automated detection -> promote secondaries -> route traffic -> seed prefix cache from snapshot + on-demand KV population. The runbook shows "validation checkpoint 2" (after cache seed) where we observe the p95 crossing our SLA threshold; we included the exact log markers.

Pricing note (short): reserved warm pool can be configured as part of Dedicated baseline (usually via committed capacity contract). For short-term proof-of-concept we offer a temporary standby pool billed pro-rata; Diego / Marcus can follow up with a quote if Nimbus wants numbers.

Please confirm if this is sufficient for your board packet or if you need any additional traces or signed attestation. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the runbook and logs.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Manager, Compliance & Solutions
Redwood Inference
